issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop, trading a truncation race for a potential deadlock.
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared and the inner while-True os.read() begins, the outer poll timeout and check_process_exited safeguards no longer apply. If the writer opens the FIFO but hangs without closing it, the parent blocks forever. Retain a timeout or process-liveness check on the blocking drain path.

issues.description: fcntl mode switch is not restored or guarded, leaking blocking state across the function boundary.
issues.detail: The fd flags are flipped to blocking with no try/finally and never restored. F_SETFL can also fail, leaving inconsistent state. Since fifo_fd is passed in, the caller's observable fd state is silently mutated. Wrap the mode change with error handling and restore flags on exit.

issues.description: No regression test accompanies an intermittent race-condition fix.
issues.detail: The original failure was intermittent JSON truncation around 86KB. A deterministic test that writes a large payload and closes the writer fast would exercise both the race and the new blocking-drain path. Without it, this bug is likely to be reintroduced by future refactors. Correctness currently rests on prose alone.

issues.description: Loop invariant, preconditions, and termination argument for the new two-phase read are unstated.
issues.detail: The cited POSIX EOF guarantee requires a single writer with no inherited fds in surviving children; this precondition is never written down. The two phases (poll-until-first-byte, then blocking-drain) deserve an explicit docstring or comment naming the invariant so a future reader does not re-introduce non-blocking drain.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler is now vestigial dead code with stale semantics.
issues.detail: After the switch to blocking mode, BlockingIOError can only fire before any data arrives, and has_blocking_error is no longer tracked. The except reduces to pass with a misleading comment. Either delete the clause (poll already gates readiness) or document why it remains defensive.

issues.description: Two parallel read loops with separate EOF semantics should be one decomposed flow.
issues.detail: The function has an outer non-blocking poll loop and an inner blocking drain loop that both append to content and both decide EOF, with nested break-out-of-outer control flow. Extract wait_for_first_byte() and drain_blocking() helpers so the algorithm follows the data: one byte stream, one termination rule per phase.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is correct and the two-phase (poll-until-first-byte, then blocking-drain) approach is the right shape for a real POSIX-level race. However, the implementation trades an intermittent truncation for a potential deadlock: the inner blocking read has no timeout or process-exit backstop, so a hung writer blocks the parent forever. The fcntl mode switch is unguarded and never restored, silently mutating the caller's fd state. No regression test exercises the original failure or the new path, and the loop invariant plus single-writer precondition for the cited POSIX guarantee are nowhere written down. Needs work: add a timeout/liveness check on the blocking drain, guard and restore fd flags, document the invariant, and add a test before merge.
